transcript:
Meeting: Lichen Analytics — Search + Rerank hosted API walkthrough
Date: 2026-01-30 16:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE); Priya Desai (Redwood SE); Marta Liu (Product); Marcus Lee (Head of Search); Anika Shah (ML Eng); Roberto Diaz (CTO); Samir Patel (PM)

[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, I'm Jordan, AE on the account, with Priya from our SE team who will run most of the technical demo.
[00:18] Marcus Lee: Hey Jordan, hi Priya. quick context — we run a mid-size e-commerce search stack, mainly Elastic for retrieval and a homegrown log-linear reranker. goal is to improve relevance on long-tail product titles and attribute matches.
[00:34] Priya Desai: awesome, thanks Marcus. we'll show the hosted embeddings endpoint for candidate generation, then our reranker endpoint that takes embedding candidates + features and returns a ranked list. also a quick tour of Console and Optimize suggestions for batch sizing, caching, and quantization.
[00:49] Samir Patel: timeline wise, we're aiming for a pilot in Q1, production in Q2 if results look good. must have SOC2 and SSO in place, and we need data residency for EU users.
[01:05] Jordan Kim: noted — we have SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs; Priya can point you to the security pack after the call.
[01:15] Priya Desai: ok jump into the API. first, embeddings endpoint — POST /v1/embeddings, we show how text -> vector, built-in normalization, and a few model options. for most product text, the medium-dim model balances cost/quality.
[01:35] [01:36] Anika Shah: how does the embedding dimension affect latency and cost? we have a 10ms P50 target for retrieval plus rerank.
[01:44] Priya Desai: short answer: higher-dim embeddings increase index size and similarity compute a bit, but the bulk of latency is retrieval + rerank. we recommend low-latency vector store (ANN) for the 1st stage and then Redwood reranker within 50–150ms for typical payloads. if you need <50ms end-to-end, we can discuss Dedicated capacity.
[02:05] Jordan Kim: the hosted plan gets you predictable performance; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for tighter SLOs.
[02:14] Marcus Lee: reliability — what if capacity spikes? do you fallback to cheaper models?
[02:21] Priya Desai: yes, we have smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; for hosted we can route to lower-cost quantized variants if there's pressure. Redwood Optimize will also recommend a quantization profile per model.
[02:37] [02:38] Marta Liu: can you show the reranker input schema?
[02:41] Priya Desai: sure — the reranker takes JSON: {"candidates": [ {"id":"...","embedding":[...],"features":{...} } ], "query": "...", "metadata": {...} } and returns scores+rank. note: transcription note — sometimes client SDK examples say "KK cache" instead of KV cache, sorry that's a quirk in the demo slides.
[03:10] Anika Shah: features — can we pass product attributes like price, availability, recency?
[03:15] Priya Desai: absolutely. you can pass arbitrary numeric/categorical features; reranker models can incorporate them via concatenated features or embed-and-fuse approaches. we include an example in the quickstart notebook.
[03:29] John (mislabelled Speaker 1): mm hm
[03:33] [03:34] Priya Desai: live demo — I'll call embeddings, then perform an ANN query (we used FAISS locally for demo), pull 100 candidates, then call Redwood reranker with the candidate payload.
[03:50] [04:20] *API demo noise* (screen share, some typing)
[04:50] Priya Desai: showing the Console — you can create an eval set, upload labeled relevancy judgments, run A/B experiments between reranker variants, and get precision@k and MRR charts. this is where Optimize flags show up: e.g., move to batch size 64, enable prefix caching for repeated queries, and try int8 quantization for the model to shave tokens cost.
[05:20] Marcus Lee: prefix caching — is that safe with PII? product descriptions have some customer-specific info.
[05:27] Priya Desai: good question. caching options are configurable; by default we separate KVS for public vs private and you can opt out per-tenant. for PII we recommend using our KMS integration and PII redaction before embeddings.
[05:45] Roberto Diaz: on security — our compliance team will want details on key management and audit logs. do you integrate with customer KMS or HSM?
[05:52] Jordan Kim: yes, we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), and for on-prem/private deployments we can talk about HSM options. we'll include the security whitepaper and SOC2 report in the follow-up.
[06:05] [06:06] Anika Shah: data residency — EU traffic needs to stay in eu-west region. can you pin inference to eu region?
[06:13] Priya Desai: yes, hosted regions can be restricted; or we can provision a private deployment in your cloud region for strict residency.
[06:21] Samir Patel: curious about cost math — can you show how tokens + rerank compute adds up?
[06:27] Priya Desai: we shared a sample cost calculator in the deck; rough rule: embedding cost per doc + ANN compute (usually cheap) + rerank per candidate * number of requests. Optimize suggests reducing candidate set or using a smaller reranker for tail queries.
[06:44] Marcus Lee: our current reranker is expensive, we rank 200 candidates with a heavy model. can we do hybrid — smaller candidate set + reranker for top 20?
[06:52] Priya Desai: yes — typical pattern is 1) ANN -> top 200, 2) lightweight filter model or simple heuristics -> top 30, 3) full neural reranker -> top 10. Redwood supports multi-stage pipelines and automates caching of KV context for repeated sessions.
[07:10] Jordan Kim: quick pause — any blockers for pilot aside from security and residency?
[07:15] Marcus Lee: labeling effort — we have limited judgment budget, ~10k labels. want to know if results will be meaningful.
[07:21] Priya Desai: 10k is a good start; Console's eval tooling can bootstrap via small-shot active sampling. we can help with seed prompts and sampling strategy.
[07:36] [07:37] *crosstalk*
[07:42] Priya Desai: now switching to failure modes — what happens if reranker times out?
[07:46] Anika Shah: yes do you have graceful fallback?
[07:48] Priya Desai: our runtime has automatic fallback to safer, lower-latency models and can fall back to the ANN score if reranker fails. also supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies you configure in Console.
[08:05] Roberto Diaz: from infra perspective we want audit logs per request and token-level cost visibility. is that exposed?
[08:12] Jordan Kim: Console provides per-route token breakdowns, per-model latency, and request traces. audit logs with request/response headers (sanitized) are available for Private deployments and with retention tiers for hosted.
[08:26] Marcus Lee: for the pilot we'll want a sandbox account and some sample load testing. can Redwood run benchmarks for us?
[08:31] Priya Desai: yes, we can run a bench with your dataset and baseline; usually SE does a 1–2 day run for the candidate and rerank comparison and share a spreadsheet with latency/cost/quality metrics.
[08:48] [09:00] *demo continues — live reranker call shows reorder and score deltas*
[09:34] Anika Shah: looks good — question about model versions: can we pin? we need deterministic behavior for A/B tests.
[09:40] Priya Desai: absolutely. you can pin model versions per route, do canary rollouts, and tie eval sets to model versions so you can compare regression.
[09:55] Samir Patel: any limitations on payload size for reranker input? some items have long attribute blobs.
[10:02] Priya Desai: payload size limits exist; for very long metadata we recommend pre-embedding or summarization. Console has a batch preprocessing step that handles truncation and chunking.
[10:18] Jordan Kim: quick commercial note — pilot pricing is discounted; if you commit to Dedicated capacity later we can credit some of the pilot fees.
[10:27] Marcus Lee: solid. who's the SE lead if we proceed?
[10:30] Jordan Kim: Priya will be SE lead, and Marta from Product will help with eval design.
[10:36] Marcus Lee: ok next steps — we'll provision a data export and select a 100k subset. we'll get back with security contacts.
[10:45] Priya Desai: one caveat — if you run an on-prem/private deployment timeline is longer (4–8 weeks) due to infra setup. Hosted pilot can start in days.
[10:58] Roberto Diaz: that might be a blocker for EU residency, though hosted in eu region might suffice for now. we'll check compliance.
[11:07] [11:10] *brief pause — screen share ends*
[11:20] Jordan Kim: wrapping up, any other questions?
[11:23] Anika Shah: minor thing — do you expose per-request feature importance for reranker? we'd like explainability.
[11:30] Priya Desai: yes, we return optional feature attributions and a tokens-level attention map for debugging, though tokens map is approximate for proprietary models.
[11:42] Marcus Lee: good to know.
[11:45] Samir Patel: can you also share a sample SLA for Dedicated?
[11:50] Jordan Kim: will include in follow-up.
[11:54] Priya Desai: last screen — Console eval output and Optimize suggestion card (shows reduce batch latency by 12% via int8 + batch 64)
[12:08] Marcus Lee: very helpful.
[12:12] Jordan Kim: recap of next steps: Jordan sends pilot pricing + security docs; Priya sends quickstart + bench templates; customer to provide 100k docs and security contacts. we'll schedule the SE deep-dive for architecture next Tue or Wed.
[12:33] Roberto Diaz: prefer Wed.
[12:35] Jordan Kim: noted, we'll send calendar invite. thanks everyone.
[12:40] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels were automatic; a few utterances clipped during screen-share moments. There were two short stretches of crosstalk and typing noise during live API demo.
